SMTO-CFG-0070 — A prompt or built-in instruction isn't in a form SMTO can use

GUID: df953134-3161-41dc-8565-93f31d1a6c27
Slug: prompt-definition-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO received a prompt to schedule, or one of its own built-in instructions, that wasn't plain text or had no name. It stopped before saving anything new.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If this happened while scheduling a prompt, open Schedules first to check it isn't already listed. The schedule may have been saved earlier, and adding it again would make a duplicate.
  2. If it's missing, go back to the conversation and schedule the prompt again with the calendar button (Schedule this prompt), using ordinary typed text. The app always sends typed text, so a fresh attempt replaces the bad request.
  3. If a script or another program creates schedules for you, ask the person who set it up to send the prompt as plain text, not a list or a number. Only text prompts can be scheduled.
  4. If no schedule was involved, update SMTO from Settings › Setup › Server updates, or run the installer again. A built-in instruction with no name or the wrong layout means SMTO's own files are incomplete or were changed.

What success looks like

  • The schedule appears in Schedules, or your tasks run, without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; SMTO will reject it the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Prompt input or template definition is malformed: a scheduled prompt is not a string, a template upsert has an empty prompt_key, or a custom default-template file's top level is not a list.

What this means

  • Prompt input is not text, a template-store key is empty or the checked-in default-template document is not a list. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Prompt input is not text, a template-store key is empty or the checked-in default-template document is not a list.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish caller prompt type, empty key and packaged default-template shape before changing template content.

How to fix it

  • For schedules, send the prompt field as a string. For templates, give every record a nonempty prompt_key; if a custom defaults path is used instead of agent_runtime/prompts/default_templates.json, make its top level a list of template objects. Existing task snapshots need no change.
  • Correct the prompt definition using the supported template format and a nonempty key. Preserve existing task snapshots.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended text prompt and keyed template definition pass their own loading boundaries.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.
